To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

recombinant von‐Willebrand‐Factor is a dimeric protein, which can be found in three different forms: a) two unprocessed monomers, b) two processed monomers, or c) one unprocessed and one processed monomer.
recombinant von‐Willebrand factor (rvWF) consists of three different homo‐dimers, and a heterodimer of unprocessed (pro‐) and fully processed (mature) vWF monomers.
recombinant vWf is a mixture of homo‐ and hetero‐dimers of unprocessed and fully processed subunits, which are not degraded proteolytically.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the molecular composition of recombinant vWf‐dimers and their subunits.
the structural analysis of recombinantly produced von Willebrand Factor.
the structural analysis of recombinantly expressed von Willebrand Factor (vWF) in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the recombinant vWf is a mixture of three species: homo‐dimers consisting of two fully processed vWf‐monomers, homo‐dimers containing two unprocessed monomeric polypeptides and the hetero‐dimers containing one unprocessed and one mature monomeric polyppeptide.

recombinant vWf is produced as a mixture of three species, i.e. homo‐dimers containing two unprocessed polypeptides, homo‐dimers consisting of two fully processed polypeptides and a hetero‐dime containing one unprocessed and one processed polypeptide.
the recombinant vWf‐dimer consists of two different homo‐dimers and one hetero‐diamer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
recombinant vWf is a mixture of three protein species, which can be separated by two‐dimension electrophoresis and that recombinant von‐Willebrand factor is not a substrate of proteases.
rvWF is a mixture of three species of dimers, which are composed of two non‐proteolysed vWF monomers, which are either unprocessed or mature, or of an unprocessed and a mature monomer.

recombinant vWf is a mixture of three species: (1) homo‐dimmer of unprocessed vWf polypeptides, (2) heterodimer of unprocessed/mature vWf polypetides, and (3) homo‐dimer of processed/mature vW f polypeptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recombinant vWf can be used to study the molecular structure of this important blood protein.
the heterodimer of recombinant vWf is the major form found in plasma, whereas the homodimer is the main form found in platelets.
the hetero‐ and the homo‐dimers are present in rvWF and that they are formed during translation and not as a result of proteolysis.
